headline: Saudi Arabia executes Bangladeshi woman over 'immoral act' allegations
summary: Sweetie Akter, a cleaning worker from Mirzapur, was executed on October 14 after being arrested six months into her work in Saudi Arabia.
details: Sweetie Akter, a resident of Mirzapur in Tangail, traveled to Saudi Arabia three years ago to work as a cleaning worker to support her daughter and family.
She was arrested six months after arriving in the country.
On October 14, her family received news that she had been executed in Mecca after being accused of an 'immoral act' in a mosque.
The family claims the charges were a conspiracy against her.
Sweetie had previously faced personal struggles, including a failed child marriage and a second marriage that did not last.
Her family in Mirzapur is now in mourning following the sudden news of her death.

headline: 85 detained as drug den uncovered at Additional DIG's house
summary: Police raided a property in Purbachal owned by senior officer Abdullah Al Zahir, seizing narcotics and drug paraphernalia.
details: A DB police raid on a three-story house in the Police Housing-1 residential area of Vatara uncovered a drug den and illegal DJ parties.
The property is owned by Additional DIG Abdullah Al Zahir, who served in the Maintenance and Repair branch of the Police Headquarters.
During the operation, police seized cannabis, Yaba, alcohol, and equipment used for consuming Yaba.
A total of 85 people were detained during the raid, including 26 women.
Following the incident, Additional DIG Abdullah Al Zahir has been removed from his post and attached to the Police Headquarters.
Additional Commissioner (DB) Shafiqul Islam stated that the officer had rented the house out online, and the tenants used the property for drug-related activities.
The detained individuals are expected to face legal action and trial.
caption:
85 people detained, including 26 women, after a drug den was discovered in a house owned by a senior police officer.

A DB police raid on a three-story house in the Police Housing-1 residential area of Vatara uncovered a drug den and illegal DJ parties.

The property is owned by Additional DIG Abdullah Al Zahir, who served in the Maintenance and Repair branch of the Police Headquarters.

During the operation, police seized cannabis, Yaba, alcohol, and equipment used for consuming Yaba.

A total of 85 people were detained during the raid, including 26 women.

Following the incident, Additional DIG Abdullah Al Zahir has been removed from his post and attached to the Police Headquarters.

Additional Commissioner (DB) Shafiqul Islam stated that the officer had rented the house out online, and the tenants used the property for drug-related activities.

The detained individuals are expected to face legal action and trial.
